example_sentences.de: Mein Bruder ist größer als ich.
example_sentences.en: My brother is taller than me.

cloze.en: Berlin is a big city.

words.notes: Also used for height of people: 'Wie groß bist du?' = How tall are you? Comparative takes an umlaut: größer.
words.mnemonic: GROSS ~ English 'gross' (144 of something) - a big number.

cloze.en: My room is too small.

words.notes: Also used for age: 'ein kleines Kind' = a young child. No umlaut in the comparative: kleiner.

example_sentences.de: Ich spreche noch nicht gut Deutsch.
example_sentences.en: I don't speak German well yet.

cloze.en: How are you? - Thanks, good.

words.notes: Fully irregular: gut - besser - am besten. Same word works as the adverb 'well'.
words.mnemonic: BESSER ~ 'better', BESTEN ~ 'best' - the irregular forms are close to English.

cloze.en: The coffee tastes bad.

words.notes: 'Mir ist schlecht' means 'I feel sick/nauseous' - not 'I am a bad person'.

cloze.en: My phone is brand new.

words.notes: 'Ich bin neu hier' is the standard way to say you have just arrived somewhere.
words.germany_context: If you are new in a German city, you must do the Anmeldung (registering your address) at the Bürgeramt, officially within 14 days of moving in. Book the Termin online early - slots fill up weeks ahead.

cloze.en: My car is ten years old.

words.notes: Covers both 'old' (things) and 'aged' (people). Comparative takes an umlaut: älter.
words.germany_context: Old furniture goes out as Sperrmüll (bulky waste). You book a free pickup date with the city's Abfallwirtschaft - dumping it on the street without an appointment can bring a fine.

example_sentences.de: In dem Café sitzen viele junge Leute.
example_sentences.en: A lot of young people sit in that café.

cloze.de: Er ist der ___ von uns dreien.
cloze.en: He is the youngest of the three of us.

words.notes: Only for living beings. For things you say 'neu', not 'jung'.

cloze.en: The way to work is long.

words.notes: The adjective is 'lang'; the time adverb is 'lange' ('Ich warte schon lange').

cloze.en: My hair is short now.

words.notes: Also means 'briefly': 'Kann ich dich kurz sprechen?' = Can I have a quick word?

example_sentences.de: Wir wohnen in einem hohen Haus.
example_sentences.en: We live in a tall building.

cloze.de: Die Miete in München ist sehr ___.
cloze.en: The rent in Munich is very high.

words.notes: Irregular: before a noun the 'c' disappears - 'ein hohes Haus', 'der hohe Preis'. Comparative: höher.
words.germany_context: Germans talk about 'hohe Nebenkosten' - electricity and heating are expensive. Your monthly Abschlag is an estimate; once a year the Nebenkostenabrechnung either refunds you or asks for a Nachzahlung.

example_sentences.de: Der Tisch ist zu niedrig für mich.
example_sentences.en: The table is too low for me.

cloze.de: Im Winter ist die Temperatur oft ___.
cloze.en: In winter the temperature is often low.

words.notes: For water, holes or depth you use 'tief' instead: 'tiefes Wasser'.

cloze.de: In Hamburg sind die Mieten sehr ___.
cloze.en: In Hamburg the rents are very high.

words.notes: Loses the 'e' as soon as it gets an ending: teuer - teurer - ein teures Auto.
words.germany_context: When you sign a Mietvertrag expect a Kaution (deposit) of up to three Kaltmieten. It must be kept in a separate account and comes back with interest when you move out - if the flat is in order.

example_sentences.en: Many things are cheaper at the discounter.

cloze.en: These shoes look cheap.

words.notes: 'billig' often hints at poor quality. If you just mean 'good value', say 'günstig'.

example_sentences.en: I'm looking for an affordable apartment.

cloze.en: Online it is usually cheaper.

words.notes: The polite, positive word for cheap: good price without saying 'low quality'.
words.germany_context: Discounters (Aldi, Lidl, Netto, Penny) are where most people shop günstig. Weekly offers come as a paper Prospekt or in apps; 'Angebot' on the shelf means it is on sale.

example_sentences.de: Der Zug ist schneller als das Auto.
example_sentences.en: The train is faster than the car.

cloze.de: Kannst du bitte nicht so ___ sprechen?
cloze.en: Could you please not speak so fast?

words.notes: Same form as the adverb: 'Er läuft schnell.' Useful phrase: 'so schnell wie möglich'.

example_sentences.de: Der Bus fährt heute sehr langsam.
example_sentences.en: The bus is going very slowly today.

cloze.en: My computer has become very slow.

words.notes: 'Können Sie bitte langsamer sprechen?' is the single most useful sentence for a learner.

cloze.en: The food is still warm.

words.notes: 'Mir ist warm' = I feel warm (dative), not 'Ich bin warm'.
words.germany_context: In flat ads 'Warmmiete' is the rent including Nebenkosten (heating, water, rubbish). Always compare Warmmiete, not Kaltmiete, when looking at apartments.

example_sentences.de: Im Winter ist es sehr kalt.
example_sentences.en: In winter it is very cold.

cloze.en: I'm cold.

words.notes: Say 'Mir ist kalt' for 'I am cold'. 'Ich bin kalt' means you are a cold person.
words.germany_context: 'Kaltmiete' is the bare rent without Nebenkosten. A flat advertised at 800 EUR kalt can easily cost 1000 EUR warm once heating and water are added.

example_sentences.de: Im August wird es oft heiß.
example_sentences.en: In August it often gets hot.

cloze.en: Careful, the plate is hot!

words.notes: 'heiß' is stronger than 'warm'. For a hot drink at a normal temperature Germans still say 'heiß'.

example_sentences.en: It will get cool this evening.

cloze.en: It is pleasantly cool in the cellar.

words.notes: 'kühl' is pleasantly cold; 'kalt' is uncomfortably cold. Related noun: der Kühlschrank.

example_sentences.de: Im Sommer ist es abends lange hell.
example_sentences.en: In summer it stays light late in the evening.

cloze.de: Mach bitte das Licht an, hier ist es nicht ___ genug.
cloze.en: Please turn on the light, it isn't bright enough in here.

words.notes: Also used for colours: hellblau = light blue, hellbraun = light brown.

example_sentences.de: Im Winter wird es früh dunkel.
example_sentences.en: In winter it gets dark early.

example_sentences.de: Das Zimmer ist mir zu dunkel.
example_sentences.en: The room is too dark for me.

cloze.de: Um fünf Uhr ist es im Dezember schon ___.
cloze.en: At five o'clock in December it is already dark.

words.notes: Loses the second 'e' when it gets an ending: dunkel - dunkler - ein dunkles Zimmer.
words.germany_context: German winters are dark: in December the sun sets around 16:00 in Berlin and it is still dark at 8:00. Many people take Vitamin D and use a Tageslichtlampe.

cloze.en: Please don't be so loud!

words.notes: Careful: 'laut' is also a preposition meaning 'according to' ('laut Vertrag').
words.germany_context: Noise is taken seriously. Ruhezeiten (usually 22:00-06:00 plus all day Sunday) are written into the Hausordnung; loud music or drilling then can bring a complaint or a warning from the Vermieter.

example_sentences.de: Bitte sprich leise, das Baby schläft.
example_sentences.en: Please speak quietly, the baby is sleeping.

cloze.en: Can you turn the music down?

words.notes: 'leise' = low in volume. 'ruhig' = calm, peaceful, no disturbance.

example_sentences.en: German is hard at the beginning.

cloze.en: The suitcase is too heavy for me.

words.notes: Two meanings in one word: heavy (weight) and hard (difficult). 'schwierig' only means difficult.

cloze.en: This jacket is thin and light.

words.notes: Mirror image of 'schwer': light in weight and easy to do.

example_sentences.de: Das Bett im Hotel war zu hart.
example_sentences.en: The bed in the hotel was too hard.

cloze.en: He works very hard.

words.notes: 'hart' = hard to the touch. For 'difficult' use 'schwer' or 'schwierig'.
words.germany_context: Tap water in much of Germany is 'hartes Wasser' (very calcareous). Expect limescale in the kettle and washing machine - people use Entkalker and add Wasserenthärter to the wash.

example_sentences.en: I would like a soft pillow.

cloze.en: The bread rolls are still soft.

words.notes: Don't confuse with 'weiß' (white) or 'weit' (far, loose) - three different words.

example_sentences.de: Zieh bitte ein sauberes Hemd an.
example_sentences.en: Please put on a clean shirt.

cloze.en: The bathroom isn't clean.

words.notes: 'sauber machen' (two words) = to clean up: 'Ich mache die Küche sauber.'
words.germany_context: Many buildings share the cleaning of the Treppenhaus. In the south it is called Kehrwoche and rotates weekly between flats; the schedule is part of the Hausordnung and neighbours do notice.

cloze.de: Nach der Arbeit war meine Hose ganz ___.
cloze.en: After work my trousers were completely dirty.

words.notes: 'dreckig' is the everyday spoken twin and sounds a bit stronger.

example_sentences.de: Der Bus war heute Morgen sehr voll.
example_sentences.en: The bus was very crowded this morning.

cloze.de: Am Samstag sind die Supermärkte immer ___.
cloze.en: On Saturdays the supermarkets are always packed.

words.notes: Also means 'crowded' for buses, trains and shops. In casual speech young people use 'voll' as 'totally'.

example_sentences.de: Die Straßen sind sonntags oft leer.
example_sentences.en: The streets are often empty on Sundays.

cloze.de: Die Flasche ist ___, ich bringe sie zum Automaten.
cloze.en: The bottle is empty, I'll take it to the machine.

words.notes: 'leer' (empty) vs 'lehren' (to teach) vs 'lernen' (to learn) - keep them apart.
words.germany_context: Empty bottles and cans are worth money: Pfand is 8-25 cent per bottle. Feed them into the Pfandautomat at any supermarket and you get a voucher to use at the till.

example_sentences.de: Der Supermarkt ist bis 20 Uhr geöffnet.
example_sentences.en: The supermarket is open until 8 pm.

cloze.de: Am Sonntag sind die Läden nicht ___.
cloze.en: On Sunday the shops are not open.

words.notes: This is the word on shop doors and opening-hour signs. In speech people say 'Der Laden hat auf.' It isn't graded like a normal adjective - you say 'samstags länger geöffnet'.
words.germany_context: Shop hours are strict: most close at 20:00 and on Sundays everything is shut except bakeries (a few morning hours), petrol stations, station shops and Berlin Spätis. Do your shopping on Saturday.

example_sentences.de: Am Sonntag sind alle Läden geschlossen.
example_sentences.en: All the shops are closed on Sunday.

cloze.de: Der Schalter ist zwischen 12 und 13 Uhr ___.
cloze.en: The counter is closed between 12 and 1.

words.notes: It is the past participle of 'schließen' used as an adjective. Everyday speech: 'Der Laden hat zu.' The comparative is grammatically possible but almost never used.
words.germany_context: Watch out for Feiertage - they differ by Bundesland. Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg have several extra ones, and on those days shops are geschlossen just like on a Sunday.

cloze.de: Ist das der ___ Weg zum Bahnhof?
cloze.en: Is this the right way to the station?

words.notes: As an adverb it also means 'really': 'Das Essen war richtig gut.'

example_sentences.de: Ich bin in den falschen Zug gestiegen.
example_sentences.en: I got on the wrong train.

cloze.de: Entschuldigung, ich habe die ___ Nummer gewählt.
cloze.en: Sorry, I dialled the wrong number.

words.notes: Careful: it means both 'wrong' and 'fake'. 'falsche Zähne' = false teeth.

cloze.en: A one-way ticket to Cologne, please.

words.notes: As a particle it means 'just': 'Komm einfach vorbei.' = Just come by.
words.germany_context: At a ticket counter 'einfach' means one-way; 'hin und zurück' means return. On regional trains, ask about the Deutschlandticket - a flat monthly ticket for all local transport.

cloze.de: Der Anfang in einem neuen Land ist ___.
cloze.en: The beginning in a new country is difficult.

words.notes: 'schwierig' only means difficult; 'schwer' can also mean heavy.

example_sentences.de: Am Montag habe ich einen frühen Termin.
example_sentences.en: On Monday I have an early appointment.

cloze.de: Es ist noch ___, wir haben Zeit.
cloze.en: It's still early, we have time.

words.notes: 'früher' also means 'in the past': 'Früher habe ich in Istanbul gewohnt.'
words.germany_context: German days start early. Bakeries open around 06:00, offices and Handwerker often start at 07:00, and Amt appointments are frequently only offered in the morning.

example_sentences.de: Tut mir leid, ich bin zu spät.

cloze.en: What time is it?

words.notes: 'Wie spät ist es?' is the normal way to ask the time. 'später' = later.
words.germany_context: In Berlin a 'Späti' (Spätkauf) sells drinks and snacks late at night and on Sundays. Elsewhere the petrol station or the station supermarket is your only late option.

example_sentences.en: We live close to the station.

cloze.en: Where is the nearest pharmacy?

words.notes: Before a noun it usually appears as 'nahe'. The superlative 'am nächsten' / 'der nächste' also means 'the next one'.

example_sentences.de: Wie weit ist es bis zum Bahnhof?
example_sentences.en: How far is it to the station?

cloze.en: The trousers are too loose for me.

words.notes: Two jobs: distance ('far') and clothes that are too loose. The opposite for clothes is 'eng'.

example_sentences.de: Im Winter trage ich eine dicke Jacke.
example_sentences.en: In winter I wear a thick jacket.

cloze.en: The walls here are thick.

words.notes: Used for people it is blunt and rude. 'kräftig' is the polite word.

cloze.de: Das Eis auf dem See ist noch zu ___.
cloze.en: The ice on the lake is still too thin.

words.notes: For a slim person 'schlank' is the friendly word; 'dünn' can sound like 'too skinny'.

cloze.en: The river is quite wide here.

words.notes: 'breit' = wide across. 'weit' = far away or loose-fitting.

example_sentences.de: Der Flur ist schmal und dunkel.
example_sentences.en: The hallway is narrow and dark.

cloze.de: Das Regal ist zu ___ für den Fernseher.
cloze.en: The shelf is too narrow for the television.

words.notes: 'schmal' describes objects and spaces; for tight clothes or crowded places use 'eng'.

example_sentences.de: Mein Bruder ist stärker als ich.
example_sentences.en: My brother is stronger than me.

cloze.en: A strong wind is blowing outside.

words.notes: Also colloquial praise: 'Stark!' = Great! Comparative takes an umlaut: stärker.

example_sentences.de: Nach der Grippe war ich noch schwach.
example_sentences.en: After the flu I was still weak.

cloze.de: Im Zug ist der Empfang oft sehr ___.
cloze.en: On the train the reception is often very weak.

words.notes: Used for signal, coffee, light and people alike.
words.germany_context: Mobile coverage in Germany is patchy outside cities and on trains. Telekom has the best network, and many people keep a cheap second SIM for dead spots.

cloze.de: Man muss nicht ___ sein, um glücklich zu sein.
cloze.en: You don't have to be rich to be happy.

words.notes: 'reich an etwas' = rich in something: 'reich an Vitaminen'.

example_sentences.en: As a student I was poor.

cloze.de: Nach der Miete bin ich jeden Monat ___.
cloze.en: After the rent I'm poor every month.

words.notes: 'Du Armer!' / 'Du Arme!' = You poor thing! Don't confuse it with 'der Arm' (the arm).

cloze.de: Mit meiner neuen Wohnung bin ich sehr ___.
cloze.en: I'm very happy with my new apartment.

words.notes: Deep happiness. For everyday 'I'm glad' Germans say 'Ich freue mich' or 'Ich bin froh'.

cloze.en: The film was beautiful, but sad.
Have a nice weekend!

words.notes: Used constantly for 'nice': 'Schönen Tag noch!', 'Schönes Wochenende!'. Also a filler agreeing word: 'Schön.'
words.germany_context: On Friday afternoons colleagues, cashiers and bus drivers all say 'Schönes Wochenende!'. The expected reply is 'Danke, ebenfalls!' or 'Ihnen auch!'.

example_sentences.de: Der Teppich ist alt und hässlich.
example_sentences.en: The carpet is old and ugly.

cloze.en: I think the new lamp is ugly.

words.notes: Strong word - about people it is genuinely insulting.

cloze.en: The talk was really interesting.

words.notes: 'Interessant.' said flatly can politely mean 'I don't agree' - tone matters.
words.mnemonic: INTERESSANT ~ 'interesting' - just say it the German way.

cloze.de: Sonntags ist es in kleinen Städten oft ___.
cloze.en: On Sundays it's often boring in small towns.

words.notes: 'Mir ist langweilig' = I am bored (dative). 'Ich bin langweilig' means 'I am a boring person'.
words.mnemonic: LANG + WEILE = a long while - boring.

example_sentences.de: Das ist sehr wichtig für mich.
example_sentences.en: That is very important to me.

cloze.en: Please bring all the important documents.

words.notes: 'wichtig für + Akkusativ': 'Das ist wichtig für uns.'
words.germany_context: Keep these safe from day one: Anmeldebestätigung, Steuer-ID (arrives by post after the Anmeldung), Sozialversicherungsnummer and your Krankenkasse card. Employers and banks ask for them.

cloze.en: These details are unimportant.

words.notes: In speech people more often just say 'Das ist mir egal.'
words.mnemonic: un- flips the meaning, exactly like English 'un-'.

example_sentences.de: Wir kommen so schnell wie möglich.
example_sentences.en: We'll come as fast as possible.

cloze.de: Ein Termin am Montag ist leider nicht ___.
cloze.en: An appointment on Monday is unfortunately not possible.

words.notes: Pattern to memorise: 'so ... wie möglich' = as ... as possible. Comparative forms exist but are rarely used.
words.germany_context: Almost nothing in Germany works without a Termin: Bürgeramt, doctors, banks, even some phone shops. Book online, arrive five minutes early, and bring your Termin confirmation.

example_sentences.de: Ohne Termin ist es fast unmöglich.
example_sentences.en: Without an appointment it is almost impossible.

cloze.de: Einen Kita-Platz zu finden, ist fast ___.
cloze.en: Finding a daycare place is almost impossible.

words.notes: Also used about behaviour: 'Er benimmt sich unmöglich.' = He is behaving outrageously.
words.germany_context: Kita places are genuinely scarce in big cities. Parents register their child on waiting lists (often via a city portal) during pregnancy or right after birth.

example_sentences.en: All the rooms are the same size.

cloze.en: We live on the same street.

words.notes: As an adverb 'gleich' means 'in a moment' ('Ich komme gleich'). The comparative is rarely used.

cloze.en: The two apartments are completely different.

words.notes: Before a plural noun it usually means 'various': 'verschiedene Leute' = various people.

cloze.de: Türkisch und Deutsch sind sich gar nicht ___.
cloze.en: Turkish and German are not at all similar.

words.notes: Takes the dative: 'jemandem ähnlich sehen' = to look like someone.

cloze.en: Excuse me, is this chair still free?

words.notes: 'frei' = not occupied or not working. For 'free of charge' say 'kostenlos' or 'gratis'.
words.germany_context: In busy cafés and Biergärten sharing a table is normal. Point at the chair and ask 'Ist hier noch frei?' - people will just nod.

example_sentences.de: Alle Plätze im Zug waren besetzt.
example_sentences.en: All the seats on the train were taken.

cloze.de: Ich habe angerufen, aber es war ___.
cloze.en: I called, but the line was busy.

words.notes: Used for toilets, seats and phone lines. It is a participle, so it is hardly ever compared.
words.germany_context: Public toilet doors show a red 'besetzt' or a green 'frei'. On ICE trains the small display above the seat tells you for which stretch it is reserved.

example_sentences.en: I'll be done in a moment.

cloze.de: Bist du mit der Arbeit schon ___?
cloze.en: Are you finished with the work already?

words.notes: 'Ich bin fertig' can also mean 'I'm exhausted' - context decides. 'fertig mit + Dativ'.

example_sentences.de: Bist du bereit für den Termin?
example_sentences.en: Are you ready for the appointment?

cloze.en: We are ready to go.

words.notes: 'bereit für + Akkusativ' or 'bereit sein, etwas zu tun'. In everyday speech 'fertig' is more common.

cloze.en: Stay healthy!

words.notes: Comparative usually takes an umlaut: gesünder. 'Gesundheit!' is what you say when someone sneezes.
words.germany_context: Health insurance is compulsory. Most employees are in a gesetzliche Krankenkasse (TK, AOK, Barmer ...) and show the Versichertenkarte at every doctor's visit.

cloze.de: Wenn du ___ bist, ruf beim Arbeitgeber an.
cloze.en: If you're sick, call your employer.

words.notes: 'sich krankmelden' = to call in sick. 'Gute Besserung!' = Get well soon.
words.germany_context: Call your employer on the first sick morning. From day three (earlier if your contract says so) you need an AU - the Krankschreibung from a doctor, which the practice sends to the Krankenkasse electronically.

cloze.en: A lot of people live in Berlin.

words.notes: 'viel' + singular (viel Geld), 'viele' + plural (viele Leute). The comparative 'mehr' never takes an ending: 'mehr Geld', 'mehr Leute'.

example_sentences.de: Nur wenige Läden haben sonntags offen.
example_sentences.en: Only a few shops are open on Sundays.

cloze.en: Unfortunately we only have a little time.

words.notes: 'wenig' + singular, 'wenige' + plural. 'ein wenig' = a little bit (positive); 'wenig' alone sounds like 'not enough'.

example_sentences.de: Im Café gibt es kostenloses WLAN.

cloze.en: The bus is free for children.

words.notes: 'kostenlos' = costs nothing; 'frei' = not occupied. 'gratis' works too. Not normally compared.
words.germany_context: Tap water in restaurants is rarely free - you order and pay for bottled water, 'still' or 'mit Sprudel'. Free public wifi is also much rarer than in Turkey.

example_sentences.de: Die Straßen in der Altstadt sind eng.
example_sentences.en: The streets in the old town are narrow.

cloze.en: These trousers are too tight for me.

words.notes: Clothes: 'eng' (tight) vs 'weit' (loose). Places: 'eng' (cramped) vs 'breit' (wide).

cloze.de: Das Wasser ist hier zu ___ für die Kinder.
cloze.en: The water is too deep here for the children.

words.notes: 'tief' = deep downwards. A low table is 'niedrig', not 'tief'.

example_sentences.de: Das Parken ist auf dem Hof verboten.
example_sentences.en: Parking is forbidden in the courtyard.

cloze.en: Smoking is forbidden on the platform.

words.notes: You will see it on signs everywhere: 'Betreten verboten', 'Rauchen verboten'. It is a participle, so instead of a comparative Germans say 'streng verboten'.
words.germany_context: Two rules people really enforce: don't cross at a red pedestrian light (5-100 EUR, and strangers will scold you in front of children) and never cycle at night without working lights.

example_sentences.de: Ist es erlaubt, hier zu parken?
example_sentences.en: Is it allowed to park here?

cloze.en: Smoking is only allowed outside.

words.notes: 'Das ist leider nicht erlaubt' is the polite official way of saying no. A participle, so it is not really compared.

example_sentences.de: Mein Ticket ist zwei Stunden gültig.
example_sentences.en: My ticket is valid for two hours.
Is the ID card still valid?

cloze.en: The offer is valid until Friday.

words.notes: Usually 'gültig bis' + date. Instead of a comparative you say 'länger gültig'.
words.germany_context: Always travel with a gültiger Fahrschein. Ticket inspectors are in plain clothes and Schwarzfahren costs 60 EUR plus a police report if you repeat it.

example_sentences.en: The milk is already past its date.

cloze.en: Careful, the yoghurt is out of date.

words.notes: From 'ablaufen' (to run out). On food you read 'mindestens haltbar bis' - the best-before date.
words.germany_context: Never let your Aufenthaltstitel or passport run out: appointments at the Ausländerbehörde are booked out for months, so apply for the extension three months before it expires.

example_sentences.de: Wer ist für dieses Formular zuständig?
example_sentences.en: Who is responsible for this form?
The citizens' office is responsible for that.

cloze.de: Ich bin nicht ___, fragen Sie bitte meinen Kollegen.
cloze.en: I'm not the person in charge, please ask my colleague.

words.notes: 'zuständig für + Akkusativ'. The single most useful word in any German office.
words.germany_context: Know who is zuständig: Hausmeister for small repairs in the building, Vermieter or Hausverwaltung for the flat itself, Bürgeramt for the Anmeldung, Ausländerbehörde for residence permits.

cloze.de: Es ist ___, bitte ruf mich zurück.
cloze.en: It's urgent, please call me back.

words.notes: Very often used as an adverb: 'dringend brauchen', 'dringend suchen'.
words.germany_context: For urgent but non-life-threatening medical problems call 116117 (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst), especially at night and at weekends. 112 is only for real emergencies.

example_sentences.de: Bring nur die nötigen Papiere mit.

cloze.de: Ein Termin ist nicht ___, du kannst einfach kommen.
cloze.en: An appointment isn't necessary, you can just come.

words.notes: 'nötig' and 'notwendig' are twins. 'Nicht nötig!' = don't bother, no need.

example_sentences.de: Das Wasser im See ist ganz klar.
example_sentences.en: The water in the lake is completely clear.

cloze.en: Everything OK?

words.notes: 'Alles klar!' = OK / got it, and 'Klar!' on its own = Sure, of course. You hear both constantly.

cloze.en: Your new apartment is great!

words.notes: Everyday praise, like 'super' or 'klasse'. Its old meaning was 'mad' - as in 'Karneval, die tollen Tage'.

cloze.de: Kein Problem, das ist halb so ___.
cloze.en: No problem, it's not that bad.

words.notes: 'Das ist nicht schlimm' is the standard friendly reply to an apology - never mind, no harm done.

example_sentences.de: Am Anfang war mir alles fremd.
example_sentences.en: At the beginning everything was strange to me.

cloze.de: In einer ___ Stadt braucht man Zeit.
cloze.en: In an unfamiliar city you need time.

words.notes: 'fremd' = unfamiliar or foreign. 'die Fremdsprache' = foreign language.

cloze.en: Finally I have my own car.

words.notes: Almost always used with a possessive: 'mein eigenes Konto', 'ihre eigene Firma'. Not really compared.

cloze.de: Auf dem Eis muss man ___ sein.
cloze.en: You have to be careful on the ice.

words.notes: The noun 'Vorsicht!' is the warning shout: Watch out! You also see 'Vorsicht, Stufe!'.

cloze.en: The crime story was really gripping.

words.notes: In conversation it also just means 'interesting': 'Das klingt spannend!'

cloze.en: The noise at night is terrible.

words.notes: Also an intensifier in speech: 'schrecklich müde' = terribly tired.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin froh, dass du da bist.
example_sentences.en: I'm glad that you are here.

example_sentences.de: Wir sind froh über die neue Wohnung.
example_sentences.en: We are pleased about the new apartment.

cloze.en: I'm glad about the acceptance.

words.notes: 'froh über + Akkusativ'. 'froh' is about something concrete; 'glücklich' is deeper happiness.
words.germany_context: Seasonal greetings use 'froh': 'Frohe Weihnachten!', 'Frohe Ostern!'. On 31 December people wish each other 'Guten Rutsch!' and after midnight 'Frohes neues Jahr!'.
